The **Four-Probe Method** is used to measure the resistivity and energy band gap ($E_g$) of semiconductors because it eliminates contact resistance errors.

- Four collinear probes are placed on the sample surface. A constant current ($I$) is passed through the outer two probes, and the floating potential difference ($V$) is measured across the inner two probes.
- The resistivity $\rho$ is calculated at various temperatures.
- The energy band gap is determined from the slope of the linear graph plotted between $\ln(\rho)$ (or $\ln(1/R)$) versus $1/T$, using the relation:
  $$\ln(\rho) \propto \frac{E_g}{2k_B T}$$
proTip: State the final formula $E_g = 2k_B \times \text{slope}$ clearly for scoring full marks.
